app_tests.why: The app's Jest shards. Turbo hashes all of infra/ into every test task, but the app reads none of its deploy and dashboard configuration.

service_images.why: The api and worker images build from the repo root: their own code and every package they bundle (the build tasks), plus what only `docker build` and the image's install read.

critter_art.why: The golden parity suite on macOS.

critter_macos.why: The macOS-only suites: real Chromium, share-card goldens, the config plugin's prebuild output.

synced_schema.why: The app may not depend on @cp/db, so turbo never reruns its schema drift test for a server schema change.

sync_e2e.why: The sync end-to-end run against the local stack.

admin_e2e.why: The ops console Playwright suite: the console, and the server code and data it drives.

ios_native.why: Native sources, config plugins and the app config always compile. Everything else that can change a native build (a dependency, a token the config reads) shows in the native fingerprint.

android_native.why: As ios_native, for the Android sources.

native_fingerprint.why: Whether the native fingerprint can have moved, so computing it for the base and for this change is worth two installs: the app outside its JS, a package it builds on, the lockfile and the other files turbo hashes into every task (a workflow change among them, so a broken fingerprint job fails the pull request that broke it), a dependency patch.
